question.text:
Let $F(x)=\int_0^x (t-1)(t-2)^2(t-4)dt$ for $0\le x\le 5$. Which of the following is true?

  1. $F(x)$ attains its absolute maximum at $x=1$
     
  2. $F(x)$ attains its absolute minimum at $x=4$
     
  3. $F'(2)=0$, but $x=2$ is neither a local maximum nor a local minimum
     
  4. $F(x)$ is decreasing on $(4,5)$
question.subject: Calculus

question.text: Let $f$ be differentiable on $[0,4]$ and suppose $f'(x)=(x-1)^2(x-3)$ for every $x\in[0,4]$. Also, $f(0)=2$. The value of $x$ at which $f(x)$ attains its maximum on $[0,4]$ is:
question.subject: Calculus

question.text: For every real number $x$, a twice differentiable function $f$ satisfies $f(x)>2$, $f'(x)<0$, $f''(x)>0$, and $\lim_{x\to\infty} f(x)=2$. Which of the following graphs could be the graph of $f$?

question.text: For every real number $x$, a twice differentiable function $f$ satisfies $f(x)>1$, $\lim_{x\to\infty} f(x)=1$, $$f'(x)\begin{cases}>0, & x<-1\\ =0, & x=-1\\ <0, & x>-1\end{cases}, \qquad \text{and} \qquad f''(x)\begin{cases}<0, & x<2\\ =0, & x=2\\ >0, & x>2\end{cases}$$. Which of the following graphs could be the graph of $f$?
